description:
The materialization architecture note describes record publication in place of the sections describing the kernel, its journal, and its recovery.

## Background

The note is the contributor-facing description of repository-state materialization. It is accurate today and obsolete the moment the mechanism changes: it names the kernel, the journal, and the recovery module in its layer map and its diagrams, describes the two-phase capture specification and its budgets, describes the expected-preimage check and the plan hash, describes the mutation-session contract down to composing the exact event-log content, and carries a session-open recovery section with an apply-time re-capture and a sequence diagram. Its closing pointer sends a new contributor to three files that will not exist.

The note is in the repository's permanent documentation set, so it is maintained. The archived copies under the archive root are pinned.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The layer map, the pipeline description, and the diagrams name the redo record and its application at session open.
- [hard] REQ-02: The capture description states one read pass with its budgets, and names no capture phase or overlap-stability check.
- [hard] REQ-03: The commit description states the write-scoped comparison, the synced record, the apply order, and idempotent re-application.
- [hard] REQ-04: The closing reading order points at files that exist after the change.
- [hard] REQ-05: The pure-producer and repair-derivation sections are preserved where they remain accurate.
- [hard] REQ-06: The core-system-design note and the architecture-pitfalls study state the same mechanism.

## Notes

Archived work products are pinned to the revision that produced them and stay as they are.
title: Architecture materialization note rewrite
